$comment: Starting values, rent, interest, supplier tiers, offers. Sections 10-14.

rent.$comment: Rent scales with slots owned and rises per quarter as the landlord reprices. Calibrated so the default 3x4 shop with one till pays the section 14 starting rent of £150.

payout.$comment: How retained earnings are generated. 'overshoot' is section 13 as written: cash is profit above target, so the target curve doubles as the cash faucet. 'flat' pays a fixed reward per encounter plus a capped share of the overshoot, which lets the target be tuned purely as a fail condition. Switch with --payout=flat.

congestion.$comment: Patience penalty for overloading one aisle. At 0 the till queue is shop-wide and nothing punishes funnelling every customer down the busiest aisle, which makes signage a solved problem. Switch with --congestion=0.35.
congestion.$modeComment: 'patience' charges crowding against Patience, which only bites once a queue exists; 'conversion' charges it against Conversion, which always bites. Measured: patience mode changes the skill gap by less than noise, conversion mode does not.

day.$comment: One trading day is this many ticks. Each till serves one customer per tick. This is the throughput knob from tuning step 5.

walkouts.$comment: A walkout is a lost sale plus a Footfall penalty tomorrow. The penalty is capped as a share of base Footfall: uncapped, one bad boss day drives Footfall to zero and a zero in any term ends the run outright.

slots.$comment: Customers may skip slots unless a rule-breaking fixture or One-Way Barriers stops them.

costs.$comment: Indexed by quarter 1-8. Cost falls each quarter (section 10).

rarityEv.$comment: Relative expected value per tier (section 7). Tuning step 4 sweeps this spread. Authored fixture values are assumed to sit at this baseline.

levels.$comment: Tuning step 1. Scalars are applied per class; see fixtures.json for the authored per-level arrays.
